answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the river checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The mesa graph is rebuilt each epoch, and hence the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the knoll audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 48 keys loses far more than 48 single identities would. That is 5 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
